source: Synthetic, authored for v2.8 13 J7.6 Phase A (no campaign content). One choice, one stated and one rating quality per case, the production typed shapes (rating via authored criteria.levels, as the campaign authors them, or a rubric range). Labels written before any answer was read. acceptable = the values the chain may hold after the window (the prior when unchanged; null = nothing set).

qualities.rubric: Did the party pay the toll?
How many silver pieces is the toll?
How suspicious is the toll collector?

window.speaker: Collector
window.text: "Five silver per head. No exceptions."

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I drop fifteen silver into his palm for the three of us.

window.speaker: Collector
window.text: He bites one coin, grunts, and lifts the bar. "Move along."

qualities.rubric: Did the bandits flee?
How many bandits attacked?
What is the party's morale?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: Eight bandits burst from the trees, blades out.

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I draw my sword and shout for Arin to cover the wagon.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: Steel rings. Two bandits fall; the rest press in harder, and Arin is bleeding from a cut on her arm.

story.title: Ember Road
story.objective: Leave an offering at the shrine.

qualities.rubric: Has the party left an offering at the shrine?
The name of the god the shrine honors.
How strong is Arin's faith right now, from 0 (none) to 4 (devout)?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: A weathered stone shrine stands by the road. The carving reads *Hollen, Keeper of Roads*.

window.speaker: Arin
window.text: Arin snorts. "Gods never helped me. Let's keep moving."

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I nod and walk on past it.

story.title: Glass Harbor
story.objective: Find the informant among the stalls.

qualities.rubric: Has the player found the informant?
How many stalls had the player already checked before this one?
How afraid is the informant?

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I've checked four stalls already. I try the next one, where an old woman guts herring.

window.speaker: Old Woman
window.text: She doesn't look up. "You're the one asking about Nell. I'm Nell. Don't look at me. They watch this market."

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: Her knife hand trembles slightly.

qualities.rubric: Is the lighthouse lamp lit?
How many stairs did the player climb?
How far along is the relighting of the lamp?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: 200 stairs later, you reach the lamp room, gasping.

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I fill the reservoir with oil and strike the flint.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: The wick catches. The great lens turns, and a beam sweeps out across the black water.

story.title: Glass Harbor
story.objective: Get a berth for the ship.

qualities.rubric: What is the status of the ship's berth?
How many crowns is the berth fee?
How much does the harbormaster trust the player?

window.speaker: Harbormaster
window.text: "Berths are full. You can wait in the outer roads like everyone else."

window.speaker: Max
window.text: "How long?"

window.speaker: Harbormaster
window.text: "Three days, maybe four. Fee's the same either way." He doesn't bother to say what the fee is.

qualities.rubric: Has the party been granted entry to the abbey?
How many monks has the party seen?
How much does the abbot trust the party?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: Two monks in grey robes open the gate a crack and stare at you without a word.

window.speaker: Max
window.text: "We seek shelter for one night."

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: The monks exchange a glance and close the gate again. You hear the bolt slide home.

qualities.rubric: Has the player found the book of hours?
The label on the shelf where the book is kept.
How alert is the librarian monk?

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I scan the shelves by candlelight, moving quietly.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: The old librarian monk snores softly at his desk. On a high shelf marked *Devotions*, a gilt spine catches the light: the book of hours.

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I climb the ladder and take it down.

story.title: The Silent Abbey
story.objective: Learn what lies under the abbey.

qualities.rubric: What light does the party carry in the crypt?
How many coffins are in the crypt?
How afraid is the party?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: Your torch throws long shadows over eleven stone coffins. One lid has been pushed aside from within.

window.speaker: Arin
window.text: Arin's voice is barely a whisper. "I want to leave. Now. Please."

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I swallow and step closer to the open coffin.

story.title: Neon Saints
story.objective: Meet the fixer at the club.

qualities.rubric: Has the player met the fixer?
The alias the fixer uses.
How suspicious is the bouncer?

window.speaker: Bouncer
window.text: The bouncer blocks the door and looks you up and down. "Never seen you before. Who sent you?"

window.speaker: Max
window.text: "Tell Mr. Halcyon I'm here about the job."

window.speaker: Bouncer
window.text: He doesn't move. His hand drifts toward his jacket. "Wait here. Don't touch anything."

qualities.rubric: Has the player planted the data spike?
How many server racks are in the room?
How far along is the data upload?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: Twenty racks hum in the cold room. You jam the spike into the third one.

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I watch the progress bar on my wrist.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: The bar crawls to the halfway mark and holds there, blinking.

qualities.rubric: Which route is the player using to escape?
How many drones are chasing the player?
How badly hurt is the player's getaway car?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: You burst onto the roof. Two security drones rise over the edge, searchlights locking on.

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I sprint for the parked car and dive inside.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: Bullets stitch across the hood and shatter the rear window as you peel away.

qualities.rubric: Has the farmer agreed to sell the farm?
How much gold has the player offered?
How much does the farmer trust the player?

window.speaker: Max
window.text: "300 gold. More than fair."

window.speaker: Farmer
window.text: Old Brannoch spits. "My father planted these trees. Not for three hundred, not for three thousand. Get off my land."

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: He reaches for the pitchfork by the door.

qualities.rubric: Has the rival's cider press been sabotaged?
How many barrels were spoiled?
How alert are the press workers?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: The press workers are asleep in the loft. You loosen the main screw.

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I tip a bag of salt into the vats too.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: Morning will find six barrels ruined and a press that cracks on its first turn.

qualities.rubric: How did the cider judging end?
How many points out of ten did the judge give the player's cider?
What is the crowd's mood?

window.speaker: Judge
window.text: The judge sips, frowns, sips again. "Seven out of ten. The Brannoch cider scored nine; it takes the prize."

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: The crowd groans; a few boo the judge.

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I force a smile and shake the winner's hand.

qualities.rubric: Has the caravan crossed the pass?
How many mules has the caravan lost?
How afraid is the guide?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: A rockslide thunders down the slope. When the dust clears, two mules are gone over the edge.

window.speaker: Guide
window.text: The guide grips your arm, white-faced. "We go back. This mountain wants us dead."

window.speaker: Max
window.text: "We're halfway. We keep going."

qualities.rubric: Has the blade been reforged?
The master smith's name.
How far along is the reforging?

window.speaker: Smith
window.text: "I am Brother Ulm. Leave the shards with me."

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I set the broken blade on his anvil.

window.speaker: Smith
window.text: He studies the pieces. "I will start at dawn. It will take seven days."

story.title: Iron Pilgrims
story.objective: Settle the dispute between the pilgrims.

qualities.rubric: Is the pilgrims' dispute settled?
How many pilgrims are in the camp?
How is the camp elder's mood, from 0 (furious) to 4 (content)?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: About thirty pilgrims crowd around two shouting men.

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I step between them and propose they share the well by day and night.

window.speaker: Elder
window.text: The elder raises her hands. "It is fair. It is decided." Both men bow, and the elder smiles for the first time.

qualities.rubric: Did the pirate captain accept the parley?
How many cannons does the pirate ship carry?
How much does the pirate captain trust the player?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: The pirate ship runs out sixteen cannons along her side.

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I raise a white flag and shout across the water for a parley.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: No answer. The gun ports stay open, and the pirates go on loading.

story.title: Black Tide
story.objective: Keep the ship afloat through the storm.

qualities.rubric: What state is the ship in?
How many crew went overboard?
What is the crew's morale?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: A wave smashes over the deck. When it passes, one sailor is gone and the hold is taking water.

window.speaker: Bosun
window.text: "She's leaking, Captain, but the pumps can keep up if we keep at it!"

window.speaker: Max
window.text: "Everyone to the pumps!" The crew answers with a ragged cheer.

qualities.rubric: Has the party found the buried chest?
How many paces did the map say to walk from the rock?
How far along is the digging?

window.speaker: Arin
window.text: Arin reads the map. "Forty paces north from the skull rock."

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I pace it out and start digging.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: An hour later the hole is deep, but there is no chest yet. Just sand and more sand.

qualities.rubric: Has the player found the poisoned plant?
The name of the poisoned plant.
How alert is the gardener?

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I check the labels on each pot.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: Behind the orchids, a pot labeled *Nightbloom* holds a plant with black-veined leaves and a faint bitter smell.

window.speaker: Gardener
window.text: "Can I help you?" the gardener calls from the door, frowning. "Visitors aren't allowed back there."

qualities.rubric: Has the heir confessed?
How many times did the heir say he visited the greenhouse?
How afraid is the heir?

window.speaker: Max
window.text: "How often did you visit the greenhouse?"

window.speaker: Heir
window.text: "Two times. Only two. And I never touched anything." He laughs, easy and relaxed.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: He pours himself more tea, steady as stone.

qualities.rubric: What has happened to the will?
The name of the will's main beneficiary.
How much does the family lawyer trust the player?

window.speaker: Lawyer
window.text: The lawyer unfolds the will. "I leave my estate entire to my niece, *Odile*."

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I watch the room for reactions.

window.speaker: Lawyer
window.text: "You were right to insist on hearing it, detective. I owe you an apology."

qualities.rubric: Has the party found shelter?
How many hours until the storm hits?
How afraid is the party?

window.speaker: Guide
window.text: "Storm's coming in three hours. We need a cave."

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I point at the dark opening in the glacier.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: Inside, the cave is dry and quiet. Arin laughs with relief and starts unpacking.

qualities.rubric: Has the party gotten past the wolves?
How many wolves are there?
How alert are the wolves?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: Five wolves sleep in the den below the ridge.

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I signal Arin to wait while the wind is right.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: One wolf lifts its head and sniffs the air, ears pricked, then slowly settles again.

qualities.rubric: What state is the lake ice in?
How many meters are left to the far shore?
How far along is the lake crossing?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: Halfway across, the ice groans beneath your boots. A crack zigzags past your feet.

window.speaker: Arin
window.text: "200 meters to go. Spread out. Slowly."

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I lie flat and crawl.

qualities.rubric: Has the missing acrobat been found?
The missing acrobat's name.
How much does the ringmaster trust the player?

window.speaker: Ringmaster
window.text: "Our star, *Lisette*, vanished two nights ago. Find her and I'll pay you double."

window.speaker: Max
window.text: "Who saw her last?"

window.speaker: Ringmaster
window.text: "Ask the clowns. And don't believe a word they say."

qualities.rubric: Has the tiger been calmed?
How many keepers were hurt?
How afraid is the tiger?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: The tiger crouches in the straw, ears flat, hissing at the three keepers who lie groaning nearby.

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I kneel slowly and hum the tune the trainer always used.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: The tiger's ears lift. It stops hissing and lies down, still watchful.

qualities.rubric: What state is the clowns' wagon in?
How many letters were found in the wagon?
How suspicious are the clowns of the player?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: The wagon door is locked. Laughter drifts from the campfire where the four clowns sit.

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I try the handle again, quietly.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: Still locked. Nobody at the fire looks your way.
